additions.title: Data protection audit framework, Accountability toolkit: Leadership and oversight
additions.locator: First control measure (organisational structure), list 'Ways to meet our expectations', first item; 'Options to consider' on committee terms of reference
additions.quote: Assign overall responsibility for data protection and information governance to the board, or highest senior management level.
additions.why: What the regulator's auditors look for at the top of an organisation: responsibility assigned to the board, clear reporting lines to it, and committee terms of reference kept under review. It is the nearest UK regulator statement that a governance subject should be a named board responsibility. Carries the 'under review' banner following the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; the page shows no publication date, so the year is the year read. Data protection only, not AI governance in general.

additions.title: Data protection audit framework, Artificial intelligence toolkit: Governance and accountability in AI
additions.locator: First control measure (privacy management framework endorsed by senior management), list 'Options to consider', first item
additions.quote: Assign responsibility for general oversight of AI systems to a steering group, committee, meeting or equivalent.
additions.why: The regulator's AI audit toolkit names a committee with general oversight of AI systems as an option, and expects evidence that senior management has signed off the risks. Offered as an option, not a requirement. Carries the 'under review' banner following the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; the page shows no publication date, so the year is the year read. Data protection only, not AI governance in general.

additions.title: Artificial Intelligence: Model Personal Data Protection Framework
additions.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data, Hong Kong
additions.locator: Part I (AI Strategy and Governance), section 1.3 Governance Structure, para 20(i), printed p.18 (PDF p.20); para 13, printed p.11
additions.quote: which reports to the board and oversees the whole life cycle of all AI solutions
additions.why: International comparator, dated 2024: the Hong Kong privacy regulator recommends an AI governance committee that reports to the board and is not confined to one division, and says buy-in at executive or board level is essential. Voluntary guidance, non-UK, written for organisations that buy in and use AI that handles personal data.

additions.title: Model Artificial Intelligence Governance Framework, Second Edition
additions.publisher: Infocomm Media Development Authority and Personal Data Protection Commission, Singapore
additions.locator: Internal Governance Structures and Measures, para 3.6, p.21
additions.quote: participation of the organisation’s top management and its board of directors in the organisation’s AI governance are crucial
additions.why: International comparator: Singapore's model framework says AI governance can sit inside existing structures such as enterprise risk management, provided top management and the board sponsor and take part in it. Voluntary, non-UK, and dated 2020, before generative AI was in general use.

additions.title: Frontier AI developers need an internal audit function
additions.publisher: Jonas Schuett (arXiv; published in Risk Analysis)
additions.quote: It is organizationally independent from senior management and reports directly to the board of directors, typically its audit committee.
additions.why: Research on how a board obtains independent assurance about AI risk management: internal audit as the third line, reporting to the board and giving it a more accurate picture than management's own account. Bears on the higher levels of this criterion. Author's arXiv copy of an article later published in Risk Analysis (doi 10.1111/risa.17665); the journal copy was not read. An argument from governance practice, not an empirical study, and written about companies that build the most advanced models.

additions.title: How to design an AI ethics board
additions.publisher: Jonas Schuett, Anka Reuel and Alexis Carlier (arXiv)
additions.quote: (1) What responsibilities should the board have? (2) What should its legal structure be? (3) Who should sit on the board?
additions.why: Research setting out the design choices for a dedicated AI oversight body: its responsibilities, legal form, membership, whether its decisions bind, and its resources. Useful when a board delegates AI oversight to a committee and has to write its terms. Preprint as read (the arXiv page gives no journal reference); conceptual, not empirical; aimed at companies that develop AI, and the 'board' it discusses is an ethics board, not the board of directors.

brief_check: Nothing read contradicts or dates the approved brief. The ICO audit framework expects overall responsibility for data protection to be assigned to the board or highest senior management level; that is a data protection expectation, not a requirement to oversee AI by name, so the brief's 'No UK law or code requires a board to oversee AI by name' stands.
